name: French New Wave
summary: Light 35mm cameras, fast black-and-white stock and real streets. A handheld camera, a jump cut and a director who shows the hand. The film talks about film.

philosophy.core_thesis: A film is a personal essay shot on location with light gear, so the director's eye and the street replace the studio and the script department.
design_principles: Shoot on location with a handheld or wheelchair-dolly 35mm camera, at 24 fps and a 180° shutter (1/48 s).
Use available light with a bounce from a ceiling or a wall, at a key-to-fill ratio of about 2:1, on stock pushed 1 to 2 stops (ISO 400 to 1600 equivalent).
Frame at 1.37:1 or 1.66:1 with a 28mm to 50mm lens, and keep the camera at eye level, 1.4 to 1.7 m.
Cut at an average shot length of 5 to 8 s (estimate; check Cinemetrics for each title) and use a jump cut that removes 1 to 2 s inside one shot.
Let one tracking shot run 20 to 60 s along a street or a corridor, and let the actor look into the lens for 1 to 2 s.
Record sound on location or post-dub it, and let the music stop or switch in mid-bar, with no fade.
Cite a film or a book in a shot or a line, and break the fourth wall once in each sequence.
anti_patterns: A studio set with a lit back wall
Invisible continuity editing that hides every cut
Three-point lighting at 4:1 on a star
A score that swells under each emotion
A tidy, literary plot with all questions closed
A camera on a crane for decoration

composition.framing: A loose 1.37:1 or 1.66:1 frame; the street, a room and a face are all in view, and the frame can cut a head at the edge.
composition.staging_in_depth: Two planes: a face or a back in front of 3 to 6 m of the street; passers-by cross the frame and are not cleared.
composition.subject_placement: Off centre, walking or turning; a two-shot of 2 faces at 0.5 to 1 m apart.

principles.rule: Use a loose frame in which a head may touch the edge and the street stays in view.
principles.value: head cut at 1 edge by 5% to 10%; street 60% or more of the view

principles.rule: Place a walking or turning figure off centre, on the left or right third.
principles.value: figure at 33% or 67% of the width

principles.rule: Keep a face or a back in front of the street, and let passers-by cross the second plane.
Drop 1 to 2 s from the middle of a take so that the jump shows, and cut on the beat of the scene.
principles.value: 5 to 8 s average shot, jump cut 1 to 2 s

principles.rule: Let the actor look into the lens once, and keep the other eyelines at 0.5 to 1 m apart in a two-shot.
principles.value: 1 to 2 s look into the lens

camera_and_movement.movement: Handheld follow and long tracking shots from a wheelchair, a cart or a car. Pans are quick, with a whip at 90° per second.
camera_and_movement.support: Handheld, wheelchair or mail-cart dolly, car mount
camera_and_movement.move_speed: 1.0 to 1.5 m/s, walking pace; whip pan 90° per second

lens_and_format.aperture: f/2.8 to f/5.6 with the stock pushed
lens_and_format.focus: Zone focus at 2 to 4 m; the background stays readable.

light.quality: Available light, with a bounce for the face; mixed street and window light.
light.direction: From the window or the street; a photoflood bounced off the ceiling gives a flat top light.
light.source: Window, street lamp and a bounced photoflood

colour_and_grade.treatment: Natural black and white with a full grey scale and visible grain. Colour titles keep primaries but stay un-graded.
grade_recipe: Convert to black and white and set the black point at 5% and the white point at 95%.
Keep a gentle S-curve of +15% contrast and a visible midtone of 18% grey.
Let the highlights burn: roll off only the top 3% and allow window light to clip.
Add grain at 18% to 25% to match stock pushed 2 stops.
Do not add a vignette, a tint or a LUT.

editing_and_rhythm.average_shot_length: 5 to 8 s (estimate; check Cinemetrics for each title)
editing_and_rhythm.shot_length_range: 0.5 s for a jump cut to 60 s for a long track
editing_and_rhythm.cutting_logic: Cut for the beat of the scene, not for continuity. Drop 1 to 2 s from the middle of a take and let the jump show.
editing_and_rhythm.transitions: Hard cut, jump cut, iris, a freeze frame of 1 to 3 s, a title card as a cut.

sound.approach: Location sound or post-dubbed sound, with room noise and traffic. The track can drop out for 1 to 3 s.
sound.dialogue: Quick, overlapping, often off camera; subtitles are not a part of the style.
sound.music: Jazz or a piano theme in short bursts; the music cuts in and out with no fade.
sound.loudness: −23 LUFS integrated, with dialogue peaks at −6 dBFS

titles_and_graphics.treatment: Plain white capitals on black or on a street sign; sparse credits, a title card that cuts in on a beat.
titles_and_graphics.type: Sans-serif upper case, 1 to 2 s on screen, no animation.

shot_primer.opening: Open on a person in a street already in motion; no establishing shot, and the first cut comes by 6 s.

positive: handheld tracking shot on a Paris street

emotion.target_response: Freedom and a restless, witty intimacy: the viewer walks with the person in the street.

use_cases: video prompts for a city walk
avoid_when: The brief needs polish, a hero product shot or controlled colour.
The piece needs a clear, closed story arc of 3 acts.

modifiers.how: Keep the handheld camera and the available light; drop the black and white, accept 4:3 video and add rules for sound and props.
Keep the black and white; shorten the average shot to 2 to 3 s and join shots by collision, not by the beat of the scene.

sources.title: David Bordwell and Kristin Thompson, Film History: An Introduction (McGraw-Hill)
Richard Neupert, A History of the French New Wave Cinema (University of Wisconsin Press, 2nd ed., 2007)
